pr_body:
Old versions of Postgres used SERIAL pseudo-type for auto-incrementing values.
Versions >=10 use SQL standard-conforming GENERATED AS IDENTITY.
This allows direct insertion of values into PrimaryGeneratedColumn using Postgres.

BREAKING CHANGE: breaks compatibility with postgres versions <10
Closes: #2215
pr_comments: Note: This PR includes updated `docker-compose` using Postgres 10. The current `docker-compose` using Postgres 9 will prevent CI from passing.

comments: What is your use case for this? If you don't want it to auto-generate, then don't use the PrimaryGeneratedColumn. If you manually set this id, the auto-increment could break on future entities that try to auto-generate an id with that value. I think it would be easier to have a separate field for the cases where you want to override the value.

I have a set of masterdata which have fixed ids, i have set the autogenerate sequence to start from after the ids which are allocated to masterdata. I want the masterdata to be inserted with the specific ids. Other data can get the db generated ids. Is it possible to do this?
I think this is duplicate of #2199 ?

FYI Postgres has different way of `remembering` AUTO_INCREMENT value. 
My PR (https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/2218) doesn't cater for Postgres database.

As a temporary workaround for MySQL/MariaDB/InnoDB setting autoincrement value for table and inserting in the desirable order is possible. This query rebuilds table and requires that no existing id is bigger than a new autoincrement value, you should probably truncate it beforehand.

`ALTER TABLE table AUTO_INCREMENT = 1`

This is the type of insert you might need to use:
INSERT INTO bar values(NEXTVAL('bar_id_seq'),'bbb')

Each time you run this it inserts a new ID +1 greater than what was in the table before the insert.

reference: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/12336789/in-postgresql-how-do-you-insert-into-a-table-with-only-one-identity-column

I have a similar scenario as @Tiketti: I run unit tests on sqlite with fixed id values for better test fixture data creation and assertions. For end-to-end tests I use mysql and thanks to the #2218 this works in mysql (what is the motivation tough to just revert the introduced behavior for mysql?)
Instead of just reverting the logic for certain database types I would rather like an option to enable/allow fixed values for generated columns in the environment (eg. just for the tests). Like this it is more transparent and controllable and you can delegate the responsibility for any side-effects to the end-user of the framework!
@pleerock What do you think about my proposition to make it configurable in connection options to allow fixed ids set by code instead of the current intransparent expections?

I'm switching to MySQL only for this reason :-(

So, is there any PR for this, and any intention on merging (or remaking it)?

Thank you Andreas, but I don't think this solves the postgres-specific problem. 
Postrgres doesn't support Identity Insert out of the Box like MySQL, or other databases do (see for example, how MSSQL does it for 18 years now, and how Postgress doesn't unless you use a bit of hackery https://stackoverflow.com/questions/21375651/set-identity-insert-postgresql)

I think we should have in TypeORM a *translation* of the setting to various DBs, even if they don't support it by default, TypeORM could just issue the right command before/after (like `SET IDENTITY_INSERT my_table ON` in MSQL or calling the next index function in Postgres) and do it behind the scenes. 

The setting could be per `@Column` per `@Entity` or even Connection and perhaps per transaction with some option/method override. 

I hope we'll see this soon so I can get back to Postgres :-)

@anodynos  are you sure its not supported by postgres, because looks like it does.  And probably @andreasrueedlinger 's PR implement it, I just don't understand why we need a configuration option for it.

Umed @pleerock thanks for your answer & amazing project! 

Well, you're both right and wrong! 

* *Postgres@9.x* doesn't support it natively, only with some hackery - eg https://stackoverflow.com/questions/21375651/set-identity-insert-postgresql. (I was using P9.6 and I had to revert to mysql because of this)

* *Postgress@10.x* supports it http://www.postgresqltutorial.com/postgresql-identity-column/

The problem is that every DB (& version) out there has a different way to enable it & use it (eg see the MS SQL Server way above). So the question is if TypeORM supports a declarative & DB agnostic way, to be able for user to enable (or disable) *Identity Insert* throughout a connection or a repo or a transaction/operation etc. 

I think one of the points of a great ORM is to expose functionality transparently of DB differences...
Thanks for your considerations.
Best Regards, Angelos

I have exactly the same problem. Both with `insert` (which somewhat understandable), but with query builder `insert` as well (even if I set `id` with `setParameter`), which is a bit absurd. Maybe just drop this behaviour for query builder, or at least some opt-in flag? I don't know.

My case is that I have separated `getNextId` (which returns postgres `nextval` of sequence) and saving entity. And I want my entity to be saved with this produced ID. From database point of view is completely fair operation, yet TypeORM is not cooperating (without explicitly writing query - because query builder is not working as well - which is very tedious and bug-prone).

Dirty workaround for me was to create serial field separately in migration, and use only `@PrimaryColumn` in entity definition (instead of `@PrimaryGeneratedColumn`)

But my primary problem is that again some library tries to be smarter than programmer.
And TypeORM is constantly being "smarter". If this can lead to bug, that's programmer's problem to handle that, not library's.

Looks like a solution was implemented in https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/8371

`@PrimaryGeneratedColumn('identity', { name: 'id', generatedIdentity: 'BY DEFAULT' })`

I can confirm this does allow inserting the id value!

It does seem to still increment the next auto id value by one though, so not 100% perfect `SELECT nextval('x_id_seq');`

Try this in entity 
  @PrimaryColumn()
    id: number; 

instead of using     @PrimaryGeneratedColumn()

also in migration do not include these  isGenerated: true, generationStrategy: 'increment'

instead just write it like this   
isPrimary: true,
 isNullable: false

And that way you can use tablerepository.save(object) function and it will take the id as well and will not generate it

A solution for anyone who has auto generated uuids, is to just swap `@PrimaryGeneratedColumn()` for `@PrimaryColumn({ type: "uuid" })` and default the id if not passed in via code.

Example:
```
await this.repository.save({
    id: id ?? uuid(),
    otherFields,
})
```
